title: Agent identity and attribution of agent actions

title: Least privilege and deterministic authorization for agents
status_rationale: Unbound defines authority tiers A0 to A5 and requires an authority registry (GOV-AUTH-001), no self-granted permissions (GOV-AUTH-003), deterministic, independently testable enforcement (GOV-AUTH-021), a single AuthorityMatrix that refuses unmapped commands (CNV-GOV-010) and a release-1 agent command set limited to reversible internal actions at A2 or below (CNV-AIO-001). Not implemented.
current_practice: Not established for any production service. Engineering agent permissions in repositories, CI and cloud accounts are not documented in any record located.
provable: Nothing.
customer_statement: Echelon's design limits AI agents to reversible internal actions, enforced by deterministic authorization outside the model, with no ability to grant themselves permissions. This is not yet implemented.

title: Reserved human authority for consequential actions; agents never hold human-authority operations or clear risk
status_rationale: Invariants exist in design: the Echelon AI-Native Enterprise Design Framework (Echelon-AI-Native-Enterprise-Design-Framework@763ff8c:AGENTS.md rule 5; src/Echelon.Enterprise/Model.fs NoAiClearance) requires that human authority is preserved, AI never clears under NoAiClearance and agents never hold human-authority operations, and this is tested in that framework's property tests for its models. Unbound requires A4 reserved human authority for grant approval and other decisions (GOV-AUTH tiers), approval bound to an exact proposal and evidence snapshot (GOV-AUTH-009, AIN-022), independent reconciliation (GOV-AUTH-014), segregation of duties enforced by the engine (CNV-GOV-003), A4 approval by a human who did not prepare the item (RR-AIN-003-r1) and board-delegated deterministic policy with quarterly reporting (CNV-GOV-008). Live payments are A5 currently (GOV-AUTH-019). None is implemented in a product.
current_practice: Design invariants and requirements only. No product exists.
provable: The EDF invariant tests demonstrate the rule inside a design framework, not in a production system. Nothing operational.
customer_statement: In Echelon's design, AI agents can never approve, release funds, change payees, clear sanctions or fraud alerts, or hold any human-authority operation; only authorized humans or sponsor-delegated deterministic rules can decide. This is enforced in Echelon's design framework tests but not yet in a production system.

title: Reliability of AI-generated or AI-processed control and audit evidence
status_rationale: SOC2-004 requires evidence as a byproduct of operations, SOC2-008 forbids marking controls operating without observed evidence, SOC2-031 separates production from test evidence, GOV-AUTH-011 bars agent-generated claims from becoming binding without review, AIN-033 treats missing agent traces as deficiencies, and A5 prohibits falsifying evidence or disabling logs (AUTH-T08). RR-REQ-X-073-r2 limits AI to extracting vendor report metadata for human confirmation. Continuous control monitoring architecture is specified, not implemented.
current_practice: Not established. In this due diligence repository, AI agents draft research records under schema validation and honesty checks (tools/build.fsx flags aspirational statements presented as current), but human review status of those records is not recorded.
provable: The build tool in this repository rejects answer units that state current facts without an implemented status; that is a first-party check on AI-drafted content, not evidence of control operation.
customer_statement: Echelon's design requires control evidence to be generated by deterministic systems and protected from alteration by AI agents; AI summaries are labeled and never accepted as evidence on their own. Not yet implemented.

title: Reliability of AI-completed questionnaires and customer-facing assertions
status_rationale: This knowledge base is drafted by AI research agents. It enforces, by schema and build checks (tools/build.fsx), that customer statements may not assert current capability unless the status is implemented, that em dashes and dangling references fail the build, and that independent assurance claims are flagged. Each record carries a history entry naming the creating agent role. Human review and sign-off of answers before customer release is not yet defined, and no answer has been released to a customer.
current_practice: Canonical answer units with honesty checks exist in this repository; human review and signatory process do not.
provable: Repository contents and build tool rules show the honesty checks; there is no record of human review.
customer_statement: Echelon's questionnaire answers are drafted with AI from a governed answer library whose build checks prevent stating planned capabilities as current. A named human reviewer and signatory process for released answers is planned but not yet established.

title: Governance of AI agents in engineering and operations: change approval, segregation and access
status_rationale: Echelon builds software largely with AI coding agents. Unbound requires two approvers, neither the author, on control-relevant modules (CNV-PLT-010), deterministic release gate rules for segregation (CNV-GOV-003), change approval and emergency change evidence (SOC2-011), and no agent self-approval (GOV-AUTH-003). Whether Echelon repositories currently require human approval before merge, and what production or cloud access agents have, is not documented in any record located. Praxis records agent provenance and has a work protocol with completion evidence.
current_practice: Unknown.
provable: Praxis provenance can show which agent produced a change. Nothing proves approval controls.
customer_statement: Echelon uses AI coding agents to develop its software. It intends that agents never merge, release or operate production without approval by an accountable human who did not prompt the change. Those controls are not yet documented or evidenced.
